## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `refusal-conditioned-retrieval-repair`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-08-01T13:07:13.153Z.

Catalog entry, by slug: refusal-conditioned-retrieval-repair

Recorded 2026-08-01. Extends the catalog; no prior entry is restarted and none is renumbered. Distinct from refuted-and-abandoned-evidence-retrieval, which scores tracker evidence that was later refuted; this entry scores nothing in the tracker at all. Its input is the agent's own failed invocation.

Gap this closes. Every relevance signal in the engine today is derived from recorded state: item fields, graph position, history, usage affinity, occupancy. None of them observe the single richest predictor of what an agent needs next, which is what it just tried and was refused. A refusal carries the command, the flag, the rejected value, the legal domain when the failure site knows it, and the nearest match. Today that payload is emitted once to stderr and discarded. The next assembly is computed as if the refusal never happened, so an agent that guessed a projection field wrong receives exactly the same context it received before guessing, and its cheapest recovery is to widen the read.

Mechanism. Maintain a bounded per-session refusal trace, keyed by the same session identity the usage ledger already carries. Each entry holds the command path, the offending flag or positional, the rejected value, the declared domain if one was rendered, and the outcome of the following invocation. Three uses, in increasing ambition.

First, domain injection. When the next assembly serves the same command, the declared domain of any flag refused in this session is included verbatim and unbudgeted, because it is small, bounded by the contract table, and provably the thing the agent lacked. This is a certainty, not an estimate, so it enters ahead of any scored candidate.

Second, repair-distance ranking. Score candidates by edit distance from the rejected value to legal values, and promote the candidate set that would have satisfied the attempt. A rejected --fields value that is close to a real projectable field implies the agent has a field-level information need, so field-bearing candidates outrank narrative ones for that turn.

Third, refusal-rate feedback into the surface itself. Aggregate refusals across the fleet by command and flag. A flag whose refusal rate stays high after its domain is rendered is a naming defect, not a discovery defect, and that is a measurable input to the consolidation programme rather than a guess.

Degeneracy clauses, which the catalog requires of every entry. On a session with zero refusals the term is identically zero and the assembly is byte-identical to today. On a corpus of one item it is identically zero. It must never promote a candidate purely because a refusal occurred; the refusal conditions the ranking, it does not manufacture relevance. The trace is session-scoped and bounded, so it cannot grow into a second usage ledger, and it must be readable without a write, so it cannot repeat the read-rewrites-itself defect the usage ledger has.

Prerequisite. The declared domain has to actually be present in the refusal before any of this can key on it. That is the discovery defect filed today, so this entry is downstream of it and is not implementable first.

## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.
